p: Monkey World is very much a place to linger. The primate groups are big and busy, and the longer you stand and watch, the more you notice: who's in charge, who's sulking, who's pinching someone else's snack. Reading the boards about where each animal came from changes how you see them, and many visitors come away with a new favourite whose story stuck with them. Since Jim Cronin's death in 2007, his wife Dr Alison Cronin has led the centre, continuing its rescue work around the world, and the team's commitment shows in every corner.

Give yourselves most of a day if you want to see everything and let the kids enjoy the play areas. A picnic is a good idea on fine days, and it's worth checking the keeper talks when you arrive, as they share the latest news about the residents. Wear sturdy shoes, because the site covers a fair bit of ground.

The Isle of Purbeck is crammed with brilliant days out to pair with your visit. Corfe Castle, a dramatic ruin on a hill above a stone village, is a favourite with photographers, and the Swanage Railway runs steam trains from Norden, near Corfe, down to the seaside at Swanage. Studland has long sandy beaches and walks out to Old Harry Rocks, the chalk stacks at the start of the Jurassic Coast. Nature lovers can head to RSPB Arne, a heathland reserve on Poole Harbour, or take a boat out to Brownsea Island, where red squirrels still live wild among the pines. Put a morning of chimps together with an afternoon by the sea, and you've got a cracking Dorset day.
